issues.message: Onboarding can begin immediately after extending an offer; no acceptance activity or state is modeled first.
issues.suggestion: Add an offer-acceptance step or decision before any path to onboarding.

issues.message: The process ends after paperwork, orientation, and training without modeling the required outcome that the new hire is fully integrated into the team.
issues.suggestion: Add a final integration outcome or activity after all onboarding steps and before the end event.

", "reference_description": "L1: A university enrollment system involves the following steps:
L2: Prospective students submit an application online.
L3: The admissions office reviews the application and supporting documents.
L4: If documents are missing, the applicant is notified to provide the missing items.
L5: Upon receiving all documents, the application is evaluated by the admissions committee.
L6: Concurrently, the finance department processes any application fees or waivers.
L7: If the application is accepted, an acceptance letter is sent.
L8: Otherwise, a rejection letter is sent and the process ends.
L9: After being accepted, the student must then confirm enrollment by a specified deadline; otherwise the application will be canceled.
L10: If the student confirms, they receive orientation materials and the IT department sets up student accounts for email, online portals, and library access.
L11: If the student is international, the international student office assists with visa processing.
L12: The student obtains a student ID card and starts creating their study plan, which includes:
L13: Meeting with an academic advisor.
L14: Selecting courses.
L15: Resolving any schedule conflicts.
L16: The student begins attending classes.
L17: Throughout each semester, the student may add or drop courses within the add/drop period.
L18: At the end of the semester, grades are posted, and the student can review them online.
L19: If the student has any grievances, they can file an appeal, which includes:
L20: Submitting an appeal form.
L21: Meeting with the appeals committee.
L22: Awaiting a decision.

"reference_description": "L1: A university enrollment system involves the following steps:
L2: Prospective students submit an application online.
L3: The admissions office reviews the application and supporting documents.
L4: If documents are missing, the applicant is notified to provide the missing items.
L5: Upon receiving all documents, the application is evaluated by the admissions committee.
L6: Concurrently, the finance department processes any application fees or waivers.
L7: If the application is accepted, an acceptance letter is sent.
L8: Otherwise, a rejection letter is sent and the process ends.
L9: After being accepted, the student must then confirm enrollment by a specified deadline; otherwise the application will be canceled.
L10: If the student confirms, they receive orientation materials and the IT department sets up student accounts for email, online portals, and library access.
L11: If the student is international, the international student office assists with visa processing.
L12: The student obtains a student ID card and starts creating their study plan, which includes:
L13: Meeting with an academic advisor.
L14: Selecting courses.
L15: Resolving any schedule conflicts.
L16: The student begins attending classes.
L17: Throughout each semester, the student may add or drop courses within the add/drop period.
L18: At the end of the semester, grades are posted, and the student can review them online.
L19: If the student has any grievances, they can file an appeal, which includes:
L20: Submitting an appeal form.
L21: Meeting with the appeals committee.
L22: Awaiting a decision.

issues.message: The process checks stock without modeling the required selection of a plastic color.
issues.suggestion: Add a task to choose the desired plastic color before the stock decision.

issues.message: The process turns on the printer and receives status updates, but does not model heating the bed and extruder before printing.
issues.suggestion: Add a heating activity after turning on the printer and before the heated-status decision.

issues.message: The process moves from receiving the artist's result directly to checking stock, without a step to choose the plastic color.
issues.suggestion: Add a color-selection task between accepting the result and checking whether that color is in stock.

issues.suggestion: Add a heating task after turning on the printer and before the heated-status check.

issues.message: The branch to notify the customer of a failed payment is guarded by `${paymentSucceeded}`, so a payment failure cannot select it.
issues.suggestion: Change the condition on SequenceFlow_16 to represent payment failure, and ensure the successful-payment branch leads to stock checking.

issues.message: After dispatch, inventory updating and shipping confirmation are started in parallel, allowing inventory to be updated before the required shipping confirmation.
issues.suggestion: Sequence shipping confirmation before updating inventory levels rather than splitting them in parallel.

calls.output: {"description":"Two semantic issues were identified: the payment-failure condition selects the wrong branch, and inventory updating is modeled concurrently with shipping confirmation despite the required order.","result":{"findings":[{"category":"unreachable_branch","classification_basis":"stated_condition_violated","severity":"error","message":"The branch to notify the customer of a failed payment is guarded by `${paymentSucceeded}`, so a payment failure cannot select it.","element_refs":["ExclusiveGateway_11","SequenceFlow_16","Task_13"],"reference_evidence":["L4"],"suggestion":"Change the condition on SequenceFlow_16 to represent payment failure, and ensure the successful-payment branch leads to stock checking."},{"category":"contradictory_flow","classification_basis":"required_order_violated","severity":"warning","message":"After dispatch, inventory updating and shipping confirmation are started in parallel, allowing inventory to be updated before the required shipping confirmation.","element_refs":["ParallelGateway_1","Task_14","Task_20"],"reference_evidence":["L14","L15"],"suggestion":"Sequence shipping confirmation before updating inventory levels rather than splitting them in parallel."}]}}

issues.message: The path through ExclusiveGateway_3 can end the process without settling the final account balance or deactivating the subscription.
issues.suggestion: Route completion through subscription deactivation and final-balance settlement before the end event.

issues.message: After a customer submits a cancellation request, no task represents the support team processing that request.
issues.suggestion: Add a support-team cancellation-processing task after the request and before the cancellation outcome steps.

issues.message: No modeled activity deactivates the subscription before the process completes.
issues.suggestion: Add a support-team subscription-deactivation activity before final account settlement and completion.

flow_nodes.name: Set automatic triggers for billing cycles

issues.message: The process can end through the non-cancellation route without deactivating the subscription or settling the final account balance.
issues.suggestion: Require subscription deactivation and final-balance settlement before the end event on every completion path.

issues.message: After the customer submits a cancellation request, the flow immediately splits without any task representing support-team processing of that request.
issues.suggestion: Add a support-team cancellation-processing task between the request and subsequent cancellation actions.

", "reference_description": "L1: In a multinational company's annual audit process, the audit coordinator initiates the audit process by sending a notification to the regional office.
L2: The regional office prepares financial statements and gathers necessary documents.
L3: Concurrently, the compliance team checks for any regulatory updates that might affect the audit.
L4: Afterward, the regional office submits the documents to the central audit team.
L5: The central audit team reviews the submission.
L6: If discrepancies are found, they request clarifications from the regional office.
L7: The regional office provides the necessary clarifications.
L8: Once all documents are reviewed without issues, the audit team conducts a risk assessment.
L9: The risk assessment includes evaluating financial risks, operational risks, and compliance risks, which can be done in any order but must all be completed.
L10: If high risk is identified, then a detailed investigation is launched.
L11: The investigation includes data analysis, interviews, and, in certain cases, site visits.
L12: After all risks are addressed, the audit team compiles the audit report.
L13: The report is reviewed by the audit director.
L14: The audit director may approve the report or send it back for revisions.
L15: If revisions are required, the audit team updates the report accordingly and resubmits it to be reviewed again by the audit director.
L16: Once approved, the final report is distributed to the executive board and archived.

L14: The audit director may approve the report or send it back for revisions.
L15: If revisions are required, the audit team updates the report accordingly and resubmits it to be reviewed again by the audit director.

issues.message: The start event states that the account is already set up, but the following flow begins by checking for and, if needed, creating the account.
issues.suggestion: Rename the start event to reflect character-creation initiation, or start it only after account setup is complete.

issues.message: There is no path that waits for an expansion release and then delivers the additional message; the process ends after the immediate confirmation and selfies.
issues.suggestion: Add a release-triggered waiting/event path and a task to send or receive the additional message before final completion.

flow_nodes.name: Give the lego sets to the children

issues.message: The “Brick sets already ordered?” Yes path bypasses ordering the brick sets, giving them to the children, and sorting the parts, although these activities are required after the design.
issues.suggestion: Remove this bypass or route its Yes branch through the required handover and sorting activities.

issues.message: After unsuccessful tests, the process returns to “Develop basic design”; at this point the required behavior is redesigning the failed subcomponents before rebuilding them.
issues.suggestion: Rename or replace the loop-back activity with an explicit redesign step for the unsuccessful subcomponents.

issues.message: The flow labelled “Vodka bar” is guarded by a whiskey selection, so a whiskey choice is routed to the Russian team rather than the Irish team.
issues.suggestion: Change SequenceFlow_35's condition to vodka, or relabel/redirect the branch so whiskey routes to the Irish team.

", "reference_description": "L1: An e-commerce company has a comprehensive order fulfillment process:
L2: When a customer places an order, the system records the order details.
L3: Payment processing begins.
L4: If the payment fails, the customer is notified, and the process ends.
L5: Upon successful payment, the inventory system checks stock availability.
L6: If items are out of stock, a back-order is initiated, and the customer is informed about the delay.
L7: The process continues once the back-order is received and all required items are available in stock.
L8: In-stock items are picked from the warehouse.
L9: Quality control checks are performed on the picked items.
L10: Packaging is done, including gift wrapping if the customer requested it.
L11: Meanwhile, the shipping department prepares shipping documents and labels.
L12: If the order is international, customs documentation is prepared.

issues.message: The process builds subcomponents through the loop and only starts all individual tests after the loop exits, rather than testing each subcomponent after it is built.
issues.suggestion: Route each completed subcomponent to its individual test before continuing to build the next one.

issues.message: When tests are unsuccessful, the No branch performs "Assemble subcomponents" before redesigning and rebuilding.
issues.suggestion: Replace the failed-test assembly task with a redesign-and-rebuild path; allow assembly only on the successful-tests branch.

flow_nodes.name: Give the lego sets to the children

issues.message: The “Brick sets already ordered?” Yes path bypasses ordering, although ordering must follow the basic design.
issues.suggestion: Route every post-design path through ordering, or revise the requirement to explicitly allow pre-ordered sets.

issues.message: Testing begins only after the process has finished building subcomponents, rather than after each subcomponent is built.
issues.suggestion: Test each completed subcomponent before deciding whether to build the next one.

issues.message: When tests are unsuccessful, the process performs “Assemble subcomponents,” an action permitted only after successful tests.
issues.suggestion: Replace the failed-test path with redesign and rebuild activities before retesting.
